summary: Hampshire County tower in Mount Tom State Reservation, run by Massachusetts DCR; registered on the NHLR in 2026; build date not found; drive-up access per the register.

facts.design: Steel, painted green, about 42 feet tall with a 10-foot square platform

access.note: Drive-up tower in a state reservation; the register says you can drive right up to it. No closure or climbing rule found in the sources read

events.note: Registered May 26, 2026; nominated by Tori Bonazoli

evidence.supports: location: Mount Tom State Reservation in Holyoke; the most easily accessible tower on the reservation
evidence.quote: Bray Tower is the most easily accessible tower on the Mt. Tom State Reservation in Holyoke Massachusetts.
You can drive right up to it

evidence.supports: directions: Christopher Clark Road from Easthampton, or Reservation Road from Holyoke
evidence.quote: by taking Christopher Clark Road from the west, in Easthampton, or by Reservation Road from the east in Holyoke

evidence.supports: DCR expanded as Department of Conservation and Recreation

evidence.quote: It is steel and painted green.

evidence.supports: design: about 42 feet tall with a 10-foot square platform
evidence.quote: It is about 42' tall with a 15.5 square base and 10' square platform.

evidence.supports: photo taken March 2026, so standing then
register compares it with Goat Peak tower built in 1928, very similar
evidence.quote: It is very similar to the Goat Peak Tower built in 1928.

evidence.supports: still used to observe annual hawk and raptor migration
evidence.quote: The tower is still used as a place to observe the annual hawk and other raptor migration.

evidence.supports: observation tower on nearby Goat Peak is maintained for raptor watching
evidence.quote: an observation tower on nearby Goat Peak is maintained for that purpose

evidence.supports: register calls Bray one of two official lookout towers
evidence.quote: Bray Tower is one of two official lookout towers in the Mount Tom State Reservation.

evidence.supports: Mt. Tom Range web page: reservation has two viewing towers, one overlooking Westhampton and one on Goat Peak (Bray not mentioned)
evidence.quote: Overlooking Westhampton and beyond, as well as a second tower to the north on Goat Peak, are Mt. Tom State Reservation’s two viewing towers.

evidence.supports: page mentions a tower at the Visitor Center
evidence.quote: Access to the Visitor Center tower is via the parking area rear of the Visitor Center.

evidence.supports: Holyoke tour listing names Bray Tower among reservation sites

sources.title: Viewing Towers
sources.publisher: Exploring the Mt. Tom Range and State Reservation

notes_for_editor: Build date not found in any source read; the register's Goat Peak comparison (built 1928) is not a date for Bray. Unresolved conflict: the register calls Bray one of two official lookout towers, while the Mt. Tom Range viewing-tower page names two viewing towers (one overlooking Westhampton, one on Goat Peak) and does not mention Bray; a Holyoke tour listing includes Bray Tower. The Westhampton tower is not named on that page, so it is not assumed to be Bray or the Visitor Center tower. Not established that Bray was a fire lookout; the register and story say lookout tower but no source says it spotted fires. A Facebook photo search snippet mentioning a Mount Tom tower was not used because the page could not be read. No photos recorded.
